executive_summary: Monday 16 Nov 2026, frozen 09:20:07 ET and reviewed 09:38 ET (18 minutes, inside the 90-minute limit). Bundle complete: candidate.json hashes to a1adda79f220 and matches candidate.sha256 and the bytes on origin/main (d07562f), is content-identical to data/current.json (CRLF only), structural-flags.json is [] and publish.py --check reports a valid structure with no flags. Official policy verified at the primaries: the Fed held 3-3/4 to 4 percent on 28 Oct 'by a 10 - 2 vote', Cook and Hammack preferring +1/4 point, with 'Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace' and 'Inflation remains elevated.' intact; the BoC raised the overnight target 25bp to 2.5% (Bank Rate 2.75%, deposit 2.45%) and the BoC Valet series shows the previous increase was 13 Jul 2023, so 'first increase since July 2023' holds. Next meetings are the 8-9 Dec FOMC with SEP and the 9 Dec 09:45 ET BoC announcement, both confirmed at the primaries. Pricing reproduces: the Fed ladder re-pulled at 09:26:27 ET prints exactly the five legs the candidate froze at 09:17:39 (0.085/0.885/0.045/0.005/0.005, raw 1.025, normalised 94.63/4.39/0.98) and Polymarket's 09:25:09 ET book gives 95.0 hike against the declared 95.2; the BoC ladder restamped at 09:26:39 ET gives 46.3 against 46.5 (H25 mid 0.465 -> 0.46), a 0.2pp post-snapshot drift rather than a reading error. Every market_validation number was replayed against Kalshi hourly candles and Polymarket price history and reproduces to the contract: 76,917 contracts in the 28 Oct 15:00 hour, 68,547 in the 6 Nov 09:00 hour with the leg 0.64/0.65 -> 0.78/0.79, 28,077 in the 10 Nov 05:00 hour (0.80/0.81 -> 0.88/0.89), 345,470 in the 10 Nov 10:00 hour (H26 0.05/0.06 -> 0.10/0.11 -> 0.12/0.14), the 29 Oct 09:00 -> 10:00 slide 0.80 -> 0.75 and 0.74 by 18:00, and Polymarket 0.655 (5 Nov 23:00) -> 0.785 (6 Nov 09:00). The macro inputs check out against the BLS API (Oct payrolls +165k with Sep +60k and Aug +186k, so +84k of revisions, unemployment 4.1%, AHE +0.4% m/m and +3.1% y/y, participation 61.9%; Oct CPI +0.35% SA and core +0.30% SA; Oct PPI +6.52% y/y), StatCan (Oct CPI 3.1% y/y, +0.2% m/m, ex-energy 2.0% from 2.1%; Oct LFS -4,700, 6.7%, wages 2.2%; Aug GDP 0.0% with a -0.1% September advance), BEA (Sep real PCE +0.0%, real DPI -0.3%, saving 3.8%) and October MPR Table 2 (CPI 2.9% in 2026 and 3.1% in 2027 against 2.5% and 2.0% in July), and BlueGamma prints exactly what the notes describe (100% hike / +31bp from 3.88% for the Fed, 53% / +13bp from 2.50% for the BoC, both stamped 16 Nov 2026). Both 9 November majors are genuinely closed: fed-h16 now states 0.64/0.65 -> 0.78/0.79 with +14.0pp and the Reuters '78% ... from 70%' framing, and the communication list is no longer the 15 October one. One defect still blocks: the notes again claim exhaustive Fed communication coverage ('every Fed communication since 28 October is accounted for') but Vice Chair for Supervision Bowman's 10 November 'The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy' at the Council on Foreign Relations is missing both from the driver list and from that sentence - the string 'Bowman' appears nowhere in the candidate. Same class of defect as the 9 November major, so the verdict is REVISE on one major; the pricing, market_validation, freshness and decision_usefulness checks pass and the numbers themselves are clean.

findings.issue: Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman's 10 November monetary-policy speech is missing from the Fed driver list while the notes assert that every Fed communication since 28 October is accounted for; this is the same completeness defect that was a major on 9 November.
findings.evidence: Fed 2026 speeches index (https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/speech/2026-speeches.htm) lists '11/10/2026 The U.S. Economy and Considerations for Monetary Policy - Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle W. Bowman, C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics, Council on Foreign Relations' (bowman20261110a.htm); the speech says 'Before our next meeting in December, we will receive the PCE inflation report for October and the employment report for November. Today, I am seeing signs that inflation pressures are persisting, while labor market conditions appear to be firming. This indicates that there is still work to do to bring inflation closer to 2 percent'. The candidate contains the string 'Bowman' zero times (grep -o Bowman candidate.json | wc -l = 0) and its notes read 'every Fed communication since 28 October is accounted for - 28 October statement and press conference (fed-h9, fed-d7), Hammack 5 November (fed-h19), Waller 10 November (fed-h17), Barr on AI and inequality 12 November (no policy content, not scored), Jefferson 13 November (fed-h20)'. The same 10 November session is already represented by fed-h17 (Waller, Bank of England Watchers Conference), so that day is only half covered.

findings.evidence: betting.fed[0].note: 'CME FedWatch, read second-hand because cmegroup.com refuses this host: 95% for 25bp and 5% for 50bp at 06:16 UTC today (FXBus, 16 Nov) and 100% in total as of 12 November against 67% on 5 November (Motley Fool, 16 Nov)'. Both are correctly labelled second-hand and are not used as independent market_validation (the two-venue rule is met by Kalshi plus Polymarket with BlueGamma as the OIS third leg), so the source rule is not breached; the numbers are simply not auditable without links, and cmegroup.com returns 403 to this host (confirmed).
